name: Pointed pen
summary: A sharp, flexible steel or quill nib: pressure spreads the two tines for a swelling downstroke, and no pressure gives a hairline upstroke.
how: Slope the letters 50–55° from the baseline and keep one slope for the line.
Press only on the downstrokes, to 3–8 times the hairline width, and release on the upstrokes and the joins.
Join each lower-case letter to the next with a hairline from the baseline or the x-height.

origin.note: George Bickham's The Universal Penman engraves the roundhand of the English writing masters, the model for every later formal script.

adoptions.via: Engraved copybooks of the writing masters, then metal scripts that copy the plates.
Frank Mason Robinson writes the Coca-Cola wordmark in Spencerian, a pointed-pen hand.
